summary: Interpreted the separation case and corrected what it refutes. CheckRun 9bb6bc3ec5884b0b824b602dd9123896 (exit 0) evaluated its comparison and it is violated with a complete witness: after polling the origin's decided index for 30.1 s the field `resync_completed_before_reelection` is false and that index is still 0, yet the fresh call still resolved `ok` with index 4 while entry 33 sits at index 2 and index 4 holds entry 35. That kills the counterevidence I recorded last turn — `decided_after_resync` is not a proxy for the ordering between re-synchronisation and re-election here, since it never becomes 1 however long the harness waits, and the shift appeared at the two larger tick periods with that field at 0 in every run. So I corrected the knowledge entry's conditions (revision 4, dropping the confound and adding the separation receipt), rewrote the interpretation's counterevidence and limitations around the corrected reading (the measured band stands with the tick period as the supported condition; the caller-visible violation is complete and reproduced), and recorded the genuinely open question the case exposes: why the origin's decided index never advances at all in this construction, which also decides whether the stale placeholders come from a late batch flush or from the truncation. No execution was requested this turn (validation reports execution_requested false); the open item is now stated as why the origin never observes a decided index here.
